utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There was a preliminary matter to be raised by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I rise in relation to the witness I handled last week, RM279. On 28th June, 2013, the Prosecution's 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 65 ter number 18589 was tendered and marked as D316 MFI pending upload of an English translation. The translation has been uploaded by the Prosecution as doc ID number 0320-2965-ET, and we thus would ask that the Registrar attach that document to D316 MFI and that the joint document then becomes an exhibit. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the translation comes from the Prosecution I take it that there's no problem with that. Madam Registrar, you are hereby requested or instructed to attach the English translation to D316, and D316 is admit into evidence. Any other matter, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: None from the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we turned for a minute in closed session in order to allow the witness to come in and to preserve the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before you will continue, Mr. McCloskey, I would like to remind you, Mr. Erdemovic, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that is that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning. Good morning everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I would like to take you and show you a short video-clip, something that you've seen before and that was not very clear in the -- in the record that we have introduced for you. It is P1147, the trial video V000-9265, and we should be starting from 20 minutes and go 15 seconds to 20:15, and then I'll ask you a question or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What I want to ask you about is this fellow that we see on the far right of the screen that is holding his helmet, which I think we should all recall we saw a flash of blue on that helmet, and he gets on the APCs a little bit later with clearly the blue helmet on his head. Do you know who that person is holding that helmet?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a man from my unit. His nickname is Cico. I don't know his real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now I would like to go to something else that you have seen. This time I think the video still we can do it. It's -- should be P1148 and e-court page 53. And you will recall that you have mentioned many times about Pelemis ordering the murder of a man in the centre of town in Srebrenica, and your -- again you have testified about this before, but it is not in our current record. Do you recall seeing the video-clip that goes along with this still?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And from that video-clip and this still have you been able to identify, well, whether this body is related to the Pelemis order?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is it about what you've seen in this -- in this video and in this still that leads you to believe -- make you any conclusion about this body and the person that was killed in -- based on Pelemis's order?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came to Srebrenica town itself, I concluded that was the centre of town in Srebrenica. That person came out of a building and said that he was not in the army, that he had nothing against Serbs and so on, and then the rest of the units came down to the town of Srebrenica from the surrounding mountains, and they began to maltreat him, beat him, and then Pelemis ordered Zoran, whose nickname is Maric, to kill that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you think this man in this photo is the man that you saw killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why do you -- how can you conclude that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this footage that you showed me, I could see the building, the buildings that were in the centre of town, the mosque was there, and how that person was wearing a green jacket and jeans, so I concluded on the basis of those things that that was the place where this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the person that you say was wearing jeans and a -- and a jacket, do you see similar garments on this person in this video and this still?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told there is a problem with translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't hear you, Mr. Ivetic. Could it be that there's voice distortion, that we plugged in in the right --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think the problem is with the translation of the English, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Translation of the English. Is Mr. Mladic on the right channel? I'll switch for a second to the -- I hear B/C/S on channel 6. Volume, right channel? I'm still hearing myself translated into B/C/S. Anyway to use another socket? You now can hear the B/C/S translation? I see that Mr. Mladic is nodding yes. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can please take this image down and go to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, you say on -- I believe it's page 854 of your Rule 61 hearing that shortly after the events at this farm you were in a bar and were shot by a member of your unit and that you had to seek medical treatment in -- in Bijeljina that didn't -- was not effective and that someone helped you in further medical treatment. Can you tell us who that person was that helped you get further medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deputy commander of our unit, Kremenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you -- where did you go to get that further medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, to the military hospital, the VMA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you get an official pass that helped you cross over into the FRY?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone who was in the army had to have a pass in order to be able to cross from Republika Srpska to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 18127 on the board.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we now see this document dated in February, the 11th, 1996, by General Mladic, and we see your name in number 1. Is this the pass you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know what those other people under you are? Do you know who those people are?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And at some point around this time did you ever get issued with a -- a fake ID?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you go to get that fake ID?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Bijeljina MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you go with any other members of your unit that also got fake IDs?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And of -- were there any of the members that got fake IDs with you that had actually been it the farm that day and involved in the executions?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Marko Boskic and Franc Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And when you went to get the medical treatment in Belgrade, did you on your own meet with a journalist?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you tell the journalist of your involvement in the farm murders?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And shortly after that were you arrested by the FRY authorities?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you soon thereafter go in front of an investigating judge in the FRY and again knowledge your involvement in the farm killings?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And a short time after that did you then come to The Hague to this Tribunal and eventually plead guilty?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Before I give Mr. Stojanovic an opportunity to cross-examine the witness, I have one or two questions for you, Witness. The fake ID -- ID that was issued to you by the Bijeljina MUP, I think you said, how was that to be used and when was it issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember precisely when the fake documents were issued, but the command just told us to go to the Bijeljina MUP and that we would be issued these IDs. They told us that we need to do that, that we had to do it. They didn't explain all the reasons why, just that we had to go and get those fake IDs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say "command," could you be a bit more specific? Do you remember which person told you to do so and what his function or rank was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the commander of our detachment, Lieutenant-Colonel Milorad Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 2nd lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it to be used internally within the Republika Srpska, or was it to be used for travelling abroad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was just a personal ID card that could be used only within Republika Srpska and in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because the pass that was issued to you so that you could go to Belgrade was issued under your own name, and I wondered whether there was not a conflict between the two documents, the one with your own name on it, the other one a fake ID.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I had to have the pass because I was going to the hospital in Belgrade, and in Belgrade at the hospital they knew my real name. I went there under my real name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. -- yes. Mr. McCloskey, you stayed well within your 30 minutes, so I take it that you would use the time to tender the pass or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've -- I just wanted to clean up what we had. We had that document yesterday that had a stamp from an old case on it as you recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We now have a new document now that has been uploaded. It's 00399985, which if we could replace that -ET-1. If we could replace that and get rid of the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So to replace the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And put this one in its place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and you can see that at transcript 13705, lines 1 through 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar is hereby instructed to replace the document bearing a stamp of the previous case with a clean copy for this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as -- on the basis of the numbers given by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the document I had just mentioned, the pass, I also have noticed it has a stamp on it as well, and that's 18127. So we'll do the same process and get that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, I'd like to have already a number assigned to it so we can decide on its admission into evidence but it's then generally understood that it is a clean copy of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I would offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That was 18127.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Therefore, document 18127 receives number P1677, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1677 is admitted into evidence, and leave is granted already to Madam Registrar to replace the now uploaded copy with the stamp of the previous case with a clean copy, the number to be provided and the document to be uploaded by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I do have the -- the list of associated exhibits. I can deal with that when you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could deal with them now. Let me just have a look. Associated exhibits. I think we have dealt with two of them, the testimony, 29019 and 29020. It is a rather long list, Mr. McCloskey. I suggest the following: That Madam Registrar prepares a list for the ones, unless there's any change, and I'm reading from a document dated the 1st of July, 2013, being the last version, as far as I understand, and let's see whether there's any -- have you used any of those? I don't think so. These are really associated exhibits. Madam Registrar will prepare a list containing the 65 ter numbers, the provisionally assigned exhibit numbers, and a short description, and we can deal with those then on a rather quick basis by hearing from Mr. Stojanovic whether he has any objections. Mr. Stojanovic, could you already inform us on whether there will be objections against any of those appearing on the list of the 1st of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this moment, no, Your Honour. We have no objection to any of the exhibits on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are 11 remaining, I think. We'll receive the list from Madam Registrar. We'll again verify whether there are any objections looking at that list, and then we'll decide on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to delete one exhibit because it was the fuzzy -- a fuzzy still of the blue helmeted person, and that is -- that we went over with the video, so I would like to delete from the list 05205, otherwise the list stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then ten, Madam Registrar, will remain to be included in the list with the provisional assignment of exhibit numbers. Mr. Stojanovic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Erdemovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is a -- is counsel for the Prosecution [sic] of Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you to tell the Court the main reason why you decided to leave the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and move to Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principal reason was that I was helping Serb residents in the area of Tuzla to move to Republika Srpska, and I was arrested for that. At that time, one of the people whom I had helped, together with his family, to move to Republika Srpska promised me that he would help me to go to Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any monetary remuneration for transferring Serb residents to Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received only money for the fuel, because petrol was very expensive. I got money to be able to tank up to drive these people, and they confirmed that when I moved to the side of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you why the Serb residents were leaving the territory of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some did give their reasons, others didn't, but I could suppose that they didn't feel safe and they wanted to move to Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How many people in total, to the best of your recollection, did you move to Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a precise answer. I would not wish to say that. I don't know, perhaps 50, perhaps 60. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How much time did you spend in prison in Tuzla on account of these activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in prison. I was in the military remand prison, perhaps three, four days. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They suspended your remand. They allowed you to go free and to make your case while at liberty.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Instead they sent me to the detention centre of the HVO, and it was then they told me that I would probably be tried. I couldn't understand why, because as far as I could understand, I had not done anything against the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get married after moving to Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get married, but I lived together with that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about your arrival in Republika Srpska, and in your statement which is now an exhibit in this case you mentioned a man called Zoran Manojlovic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you to tell us who Zoran Manojlovic is, and how did you see his role in the establishment of the unit that you joined?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to Bijeljina, that person of Serb ethnicity whom I had helped move from the area controlled by the BH Army and the HVO did not keep the promise to help me move abroad from Yugoslavia, move to Switzerland. He had promised that to me and the girlfriend I was living with at the time. In Republika Srpska a mobilisation was underway, and everyone who was fit to serve in the army had to join. First of all, from Republika Srpska some men in some units started to mistreat me, tell me that I couldn't stay there, that I had to join the army. So from Republika Srpska I went to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me stop you here for a moment. My question was: How did you make contact with Zoran Manojlovic, and who is he, and what was his role?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made contact with Zoran Manojlovic because individuals of Croat ethnicity had already been in contact with Zoran Manojlovic, and as far as I was able to see, he was the commander of that unit that consisted of six Croats, one Slovene, and one Muslim. That was a unit attached to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were they physically located when you joined that group of six or seven men?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Dvorovi near Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could counsel speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you speak into the microphone when you put questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. I will try this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what did Zoran Manojlovic tell you? What kind of unit was that, and what were your tasks to be?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before making contact with Zoran Manojlovic I had spoken to two or three Croats I had known from before from Tuzla, and they told me that it would be a sabotage unit that would go behind enemy lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Zoran Manojlovic have rank, and what was his relationship to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, they addressed him as Captain. I don't know if that was his real rank, but I know that he was in contact with Colonel Petar Salapura.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time before June 1995, you as a unit receive directly any assignments or orders from Petar Salapura, or did all the orders come through your commanders?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through our commanders. All the orders I received were received through the commanders of our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were sent for training in the tasks that this unit was meant for?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Individuals from my unit did go, but at that time I didn't go for the training in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the relationship between Zoran Manojlovic and that multi-ethnic unit? What was his attitude to this multi-ethnic unit and you personally?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was friendly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You personally had no problems with Zoran Manojlovic while he was commander of that unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point there occurred a change in the command staff, and 2nd Lieutenant Pelemis became your commander. Can you tell me when?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that was in 1994, in October, I think, but I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After Pelemis arrived, did your unit get or second platoon based in Dragasevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that when Pelemis arrived there occurred a change in the method of operation and the method of employment of that unit to which you belonged?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court what kind of change occurred.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the unit was expanded, as you already mentioned. Candidates were inducted into the unit from all areas of Republika Srpska, including the Vlasenica platoon. They were an assault brigade of sorts. They did not hold positions on the front line. They carried out sabotage actions. So in that sense, our unit sometimes went to hold positions on the front line above Sekovici, whereas the platoon from Bijeljina did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a change in the commander's attitude towards you as a non-Serb component of the unit that he commanded?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not going to speak for other people. It's up to them to say what their relationship with Pelemis was like, but my relationship with him was not so good.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As a person who established that unit, Zoran Manojlovic wanted to have a multi-ethnic, multinational unit as a part of the Army of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was his purpose, his objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That assumes a fact not in evidence, that he actually established the unit to the degree he's referring to the testimony, fine, but establishing the unit is a fairly significant thing that we have not seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do you accept that that's not yet been established? You were asking about the attitude of the person you mentioned in relation to the multi-ethnicity of the unit irrespective of whether he could be -- could be called the person who established it. And could you then respond to that question, Witness, which is whether Mr. Manojlovic wanted to have a multi-ethnic, multinational unit -- oh, you have answered that already. Yes. Yes. I missed that. Mr. Stojanovic, next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you to the Prosecutor as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you this, perhaps you can give an answer. This idea of a multi-ethnic unit, was that an idea that Zoran Manojlovic implemented and it was the idea of the Main Staff, or was it his idea that he propose to Salapura and the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never discussed this with Zoran Manojlovic, so I'm not able to answer this question, unfortunately. All I can say is that it was his idea to have a special unit, but I don't think that he thought about the personnel or the ethnic belonging of -- of the members. He just wanted to have a special unit, and this is something that we would talk about when he came to the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in the question, Witness, mention was made both of Mr. Manojlovic and of the Main Staff. Let me just see whether I understood it. You mean that even for Mr. Manojlovic it is true that he just wanted to have a special unit irrespective of its ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In order to avoid any contradictions for the transcript, I just wanted to ask you again. You said what the position was of Stojanovic [as interpreted] regarding the ethnic composition. Could you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he had a friendly attitude. I said earlier that this was not important to him who was of what ethnicity. This was something that he never demonstrated in relation to me or others. I don't know what his personal opinion is what he -- his thoughts were in his head compared to what he was telling us. I'm just saying what his conduct was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my colleague has just drawn my attention to the fact that a wrong name was recorded. Instead of "Stojanovic" -- instead of "Manojlovic" it says "Stojanovic." This is page 17, line 23. So I just wanted to clarify that in order to prevent any kind of mistakes or misunderstandings in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Where you referred to the position taken by Mr. -- logically Mr. Manojlovic, the transcript reads "Stojanovic," but also with a sign that it will be reviewed after this session. That is clear. You've received an answer to your question, Mr. -- yes, you've received an answer to that question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to move to specific questions that relate to the events in Srebrenica. Your first assignment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you do so, could I put one follow-up question to the witness. You said the unit was later expanded. Now, those, if I could say so, the newcomers, were they Serbs, or were they Croats or Muslims or a mixture? So I'm not talking about the original composition, but you said a team, the unit expanded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the other persons who joined our units were -- our unit were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the topic of the action in the second half of June 1995 and the entry into the town of Srebrenica, this is something that you already testified about. I just wanted to ask you a few things. Could you remember the specific task that you were given?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning when I came to the barracks in Bijeljina, I was told that we were going out on an assignment. We were told to go and -- to go home, to take another uniform, and to return to the barracks right away because we were going out on an assignment. And then when we came back, when we started to put the things and the weapons in the bus, they told us that we were going in the direction of Bratunac and that they -- we -- there we would meet up with the Vlasenica platoon. When we came to Bratunac, the persons were not there yet from the Vlasenica platoon, so we were told to wait there for the whole unit to assemble. I don't know how long we spent there. The unit from Vlasenica arrived, the platoon, and then they told us after that that we should board trucks and go in the direction of Srebrenica. We went to Srebrenica from Bratunac through woods and mountains in our military vehicles. In the evening on the 10th, we came to the outskirts of Srebrenica, to an elevation, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just ask you to pause here for a moment and then we will continue on this topic but just one more thing before the break. In the second half of June there was an action directed at the centre of Srebrenica through the mine. What was the task that you were given, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were supposed to enter Srebrenica through the mine and to try to disrupt the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, their soldiers who were in Srebrenica, so that we would get them to surrender to the Army of Republika Srpska, to surrender and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get the order from the commander of your unit, Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did this order contain any instructions regarding the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you told at which facilities your actions were supposed to be directed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way they explained it, they said where the Naser Oric command was in Srebrenica. They thought that it was located -- and they told us where they thought the troops and the police were located in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the task was to carry out actions against the facilities of the army and police in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How many people took part in the action?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the precise number, but I think it was most of our unit, both from Bijeljina and the contingent from Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long was the action once you came out of the mine?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't stay long, perhaps 20 minutes. Only two shells were fired from hand-held shoulder borne weapons. Perhaps there are a few shots from an automatic rifle and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this is a good moment for the break, and then we will continue with another document after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will do that, but before we take the break, could I ask you to clarify your last answer. You said you didn't stay long. Only two shells were fired from a hand-held shoulder borne weapons and a few shots from automatic rifles. Are you talking about fire by your units or your troops, or are you talking about fire -- incoming fire from the enemy side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There was no enemy fire. We were the ones who fired, the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One -- one follow-up question, just briefly. What was the target you fired at or the members of your unit fired at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I already said, at two locations where our commander explained to us the Bratunac unit brigade members were who helped us get through the Bratunac tunnel, they were familiar with the tunnel, they explained where the Naser Oric command was and where the police station was and the army. The shells were fired at those two facilities. Grenades were fired at each one of those facilities, and then automatic rifle fire was opened, but this is not something that lasted a very long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Were these buildings typical military buildings, barracks or something like that, or how can you describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think one of the buildings was just a regular buildings, like a normal building, and the other facility was a hangar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will take the break, but not until after the witness has left the courtroom, but we first need to go into closed session for that purpose, and we'll resume in closed session at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, before the break you mentioned it. Can you please tell us the weapons from which those two projectiles were fired?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were two zoljas, hand-held launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us how long it took you to pass through the mine pit, through the tunnel that you passed through?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but it did take a while. I think it took over two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the fire from the zolja, was that fired by your unit or the Vlasenica unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was members of our unit who fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You received orders from your commander, Pelemis, in the course of the action itself, right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was there with us as we were going through the mine. We received our orders before we entered the mine. They told us what needed to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I stop for a moment, it's because I'm just waiting for the interpretation, because we speak the same language. So don't worry about that. In the Army of Republika Srpska, did you have any training regarding the tasks that you were performing?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where and what kind of training?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning when we were just the eight of us in the unit, we underwent training from an officer who was in our unit. He was a former JNA officer, and he was a sabotage operative. He taught us to use explosives and other things. This took place in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After Zoran Manojlovic left, this officer stopped working with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And in the JNA, did you have any kind of specialist training about the use of explosives, dynamite, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You already had combat experience from Vukovar; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you serve your regular military service -- correction: Where did you serve around Vukovar? Where was that combat?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honestly, I can't believe [as interpreted] the place close to Vukovar where we were based.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or in the HVO, did you undergo any specialised training as to how to use explosives and how to conduct sabotage operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were with that unit, did you receive a military rank?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the unit was expanded, I was commander of the first group in the Bijeljina Platoon. I had the rank of sergeant. However, due to a disagreement with Pelemis, I was stripped of that rank later. I became a private again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer to the last question, we find that in the -- in the testimony which was admitted into evidence, and for all the previous questions the Chamber is lost as far as the relevance is concerned. I mean, whether you are trained in explosives, yes or no, seems to be rather far away from what the Prosecution is dealing with in the evidence presented, that is to participate in executions of persons who were unloaded from buses by the hundreds. So therefore, we do not see whether to be trained or not to be trained in -- in explosives plays any role in that, but if you could make it clear to us, then please do it with such focused questions that we are able to follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I shall do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me, when were you stripped of the rank of sergeant?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly when, but I know there was a difference of opinions between me and Pelemis, because I had said that an operation could not be carried out because it would cause civilian casualties. Pelemis did not believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up in e-court 65 ter 05677.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have the document before you, and I should like us to look at it together. Before the break you were saying that on the 10th of July you set out to carry out the task related to Srebrenica. We see at the top: "Pursuant to the order of the Republika Srpska Army Main Staff - Intelligence Sector, strictly confidential number 12/45-852," dated "10 July 1995, "related to the movement of the elements of the unit, I hereby order." The first thing I want to ask you: Did you ever see this order coming from the intelligence sector of the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecutor showed it to me when I testified in the Karadzic case, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember who signed this document ordering the movement?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milorad Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know who signed the order originating from the intelligence sector of the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean do I know who signed it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to put this question differently. Who issued assignments to Milorad Pelemis as the commander of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I was able to see and find out, it was Colonel Petar Salapura.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this document you have before you, it says that it was the commander, 2nd Lieutenant Milorad Pelemis, who ordered elements of your unit to move. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But please look, who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milorad Pelemis, 2nd lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see the end of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Your Honour. We need to see the end of the document and zoom in on the signature and stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then when you take a better look, can you see that this signature is by Franc Kos, and it says, "For the commander"?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is how Franc Kos signed himself, but I can see in English that it's signed by Franc Kos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about the signature, who signed this document? Apparently you are -- Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- I really don't know. I just would go on what the witnesses say. I have no reason to disbelieve the CLSS's reading of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, tell us what were the responsibilities, the duties of Franc Kos in your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Bijeljina Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Before we go on, could we agree that this document can come into evidence so we don't forget?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you want to tender this, Mr. -- we'll then wait until the Defence deems the time there to -- to do it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How does one realise -- find out from the B/C/S version that this is signed by Franc Kos? Well, I see the signature, yes. Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That is why I wanted us to zoom in on this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Franc Kos had authority from your commander to sign such orders on his behalf?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at the same page on the B/C/S but zoom out and see the first page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Here under number 7 we see your name, and it is indicated that at that moment, on the 10th of July, you were a sergeant. Does this change your earlier position that at that time you had no particular duties or rank?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've always said, I did not see this document then, and I can only tell you what my unit commander had told me, that he had no trust in me, that I'm not a sergeant, and I was never told that I would become a sergeant again. Only later at some celebration of our unit at Dragasevac, footage of which I was shown by the Prosecutor, that was the time when I got the rank of sergeant, in August-September 1995. And my contract also says that I'm a sergeant. This document says that I'm a sergeant. And then they tell me that I got the rank of sergeant only in July or August 1995. That's what's shown on that footage. I don't know why that happened, but after that operation that I refused to carry out, I was told by my commander that I was no longer going to be a sergeant and no longer going to be the commander of our group in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that what you are saying runs counter to all the documents you've mentioned, the contract that you signed, the order dated the 10th of July, and the video recording of that celebration and the awarding of decorations where you were indicated as a sergeant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That doesn't make logical sense, and it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it's logical or not, you're referring to a ceremony, Mr. Stojanovic. Could I first hear from you what ceremony exactly you are referring to. The order is clear, appointment -- we also understand what you're referring to. Whether it's logical or not is a different matter, but the ceremony was -- Mr. Stojanovic, which ceremony?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the recording of that ceremony is on the Prosecution exhibit list. The witness has answered, and I can answer. That was the ceremony of celebration, and the recording shows the 10th Sabotage Detachment and the decorations awarded to them. And that video recording is 65 ter, on the Prosecution list -- just a moment I'm trying to locate this video-clip. I believe it's 65 ter 22290. And it was already used in the other case where this gentleman testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it been used in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I had not planned to play it, but we can play it very easily, and -- but my objection was based on the fact that this -- my recollection of the video shows that he's promoted to sergeant, not that he is sergeant. So it's absolutely against what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I'd like to deal with my problem first and then if you would not mind deal with the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if this is a video which is played in another case, don't expect the Chamber to be aware of it if it's not admitted, and it apparently is not in any way. So therefore, if you want to ask a question about the logic and referring to other evidential material, you should take care that the Chamber is aware of that material so they can follow your logic or lack of logic, especially when Mr. McCloskey thinks that you are misrepresenting what is found on that video. Please proceed. Mr. McCloskey, does that deal with the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I would say perhaps misinterpreting. I -- I'm -- and my memory is not always perfect. Mr. Stojanovic and I rarely disagree, but my point is that it was consistent with what the witness said, not with his conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, another matter arises: To what extent being promoted or demoted or being appointed in those positions is really the core of the testimony of this witness or whether it is just an element in the margin, because whether you participate as a demoted sergeant or someone to be promoted as a sergeant in the execution of people unloaded from buses, and that's the evidence the Prosecution presents, may be a marginal issue on the whole matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you this way then: Is it correct that the document you have before you and the contract whereby you were inducted into the Army of Republika Srpska for an indefinite time as a sergeant runs counter to what you've said today, namely that in July 1995, you were not a sergeant?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I say this to you? What is the best way to tell you this? I don't know. I didn't see this document until I testified in the Karadzic case. The Prosecutor asked me, just as you are asking me, the same question, and then we watched that footage, and then I explained what Pelemis did. I knew that according to the contract I was a sergeant, but he told me at one point that I was no longer a sergeant or a commander of one group in the Bijeljina Platoon, and then I saw that video recording from late 1995. I saw that they gave me the rank of sergeant only then. So I don't know what you make out of that, whether I was a sergeant or not a sergeant. I saw on the video-clip that it was only then they gave me that rank. I cannot explain it any better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the witness has at least been clear that he didn't remember exactly when he was stripped of the rank of sergeant. Page 25, line 9, "Just tell me, when were you stripped of the rank of sergeant?" The witness says: I have no clear recollection of that. I can't remember exactly. So therefore, the witness has at least shown that being appointed and then being stripped of is something which happened but without details as to when exactly. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We will come back to the 10th. In the evening you were in the wider Srebrenica area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The night of the 10th to the 11th, there were no combat actions or contact with the BiH Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th you received a new combat assignment, and I would like to ask you to tell us what it was according to your best recollection.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th, in the morning, the commander of our unit told us that we would be the first unit to get into the town and that we would be assigned some 15 people from the Drina Wolves, and he told us that we should not fire at the civilian population and that we should be directing the civilian population, if they were still in their homes, that we should call them to come out of their houses and go to the football stadium in Srebrenica. I don't know where the stadium is, but that's what they told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you at any point find yourself close to the positions that were bombed by the NATO Air Force?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you reach the first houses of Srebrenica before the NATO bombing commenced?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had reached the first houses, and that was when one or two bombs exploded at an elevation close to us, above us, as far as I can remember. They were dropped by NATO planes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And under whose command were you at that specific point in time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milorad Pelemis was there with us in the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were there any members of the unit noted in the order that you have in front of you, with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the group that was going towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is a good time, since I'm not going to be using this document anymore, to tender it. It's 65 ter document 05677.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, I do understand. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 05677 receives number D320, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Up until that point when you reached Srebrenica, were you able to see or hear General Ratko Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know if he was in that area at all until the next order that you received relating to General Ratko Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After entering Srebrenica, you received a new order from your commander, Pelemis. You received -- you personally received this order. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what kind of an order it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three other members of my unit and I received an order to go back to the entrance on the outskirts of Srebrenica, and we were told that we should form a check-point there and wait for General Mladic to pass, and when he passed that check-point, we would need to inform our unit commander about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The incident with the killing of a male that you talked about by a man nicknamed Maljic had already occurred before General Mladic arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did you wait at this newly set-up check-point before General Mladic passed by?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember precisely, but I think it was one to two hours. I cannot give you a precise answer about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And was there any combat underway during that time, shooting, clashes, or anything that would indicate that the warring sides were in combat?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no combat activities, there was no fire. Perhaps in the nearby woods you could hear shooting above Milici and so on, but in the town itself there were no combat actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you have an explanation that you could provide to the Trial Chamber and to us regarding the fact that Pelemis said, "Go to Srebrenica. Don't fire at civilians," and so on and so forth, but then an hour or two later he then issued an order that a man be killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain that to you. How can I explain that? I cannot. I didn't understand that myself. I know that it's incomprehensible when you tell someone who was not a part of that war about, you know, someone who would say not to touch civilians and then an hour later would say that a civilian should be killed. I cannot explain that, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will rephrase the question or put it in a different way. You personally, did you take it very seriously when he issued an order that you were not to kill civilians? Did you yourself take that order seriously?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And even without Pelemis's order, I as a soldier, would not touch civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As General Mladic was passing by, did he stop at the place where you were or did he just pass the check-point?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't stop there. They passed, as far as I can remember. Mr. Mladic was in a Puh vehicle of the ex-JNA, the Army of Yugoslavia. There was also a Praga there and I think another vehicle, but I cannot remember it all exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far was Pelemis from where you were when you reported that General Mladic had passed by?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he issued that order that we should go back to the place where we entered the town, he was in the centre of town. So I cannot tell you precisely where Pelemis was at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see if at any point in time Pelemis reported or briefed General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That evening - now we will proceed faster - and that night, you spent in facilities in the town of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And there were no combat actions, and you did not take part in any fighting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 11th we were told that we would remain in Srebrenica because we had passed through the mine. So we were told that we would be searching the mine. So when Pelemis came on the 12th, he said that this did not need to be done, and then in the course of the 11th, during the evening and the night, there were no combat actions in the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that at the point in time when the Army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica there was no longer any civilian population in Srebrenica as they had all abandoned the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them had left. When we were calling on people to leave their houses, there were perhaps 100 or 200 persons who responded, and they were mostly elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And what was the conduct towards those persons you found in those abandoned houses in the abandoned town, your conduct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us in our unit told them that they should walk in front of us and go to the football stadium. I don't know where the football pitch was. I don't know if it existed or not, but anyway, that's where we directed them to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, at some point you set off towards your headquarters, and you did not pass through Potocari and Bratunac. Would that be correct what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you told why you should not go along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje-Milici route but should take a different route?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we were told that that road was still not -- I'm trying to find the words in our language, but it's hard, because the road had still not been secured, that there was still fighting on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Because a vehicle broke down, it was only on the night of the 12th to the 13th that you reached your base again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then the following two days you attended the funeral of your colleague Koljivrat who was killed. The funeral was in Trebinje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now we come to the 16th, in the morning. I would like to ask you, if you are able to remember, who was at the base in Dragasevac when you returned from Trebinje that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the people from the Bijeljina Platoon were there, and then also some troops from the Vlasenica platoon. When we came back from Trebinje in the morning, they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your colleague Koljivrat was killed in a traffic accident on his return from Srebrenica on the 12th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And your unit commander was also injured in the accident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And on the 16th of July in the morning, did you see him anywhere at the unit command?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see him in Dragasevac on the 16th of July. He had a Band-Aid on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And who specifically issued orders to you on the 16th in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th in the morning Brano Gojkovic came to the premises where we were sleeping, where our beds were in Dragasevac, and he said that I, Zoran Gorenje and Franc Kos should take our weapons and proceed for an action as ordered by Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now we come to the question which prompted us to deal with your rank. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber who Brano Gojkovic is.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brano Gojkovic is a soldier from the Vlasenica platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can a soldier from a different platoon issue an order, an executive order, to you or to Franc Kos who at the time was a lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our unit it was possible, because if the commander of our unit assigned him to be the commander of the squad for that assignment, then he could issue an order to me or to anyone else that Pelemis assigned to that particular action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see or hear Pelemis issue to him an order that he was supposed to pass on to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Practically you took his word for it, that it was an order from Pelemis that he was just passing on. Is that a correct conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Gojkovic mention you by name when he said it was Pelemis's order that you should go into a new mission?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know a member of your unit called Dragan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked about that name when I testified in the Karadzic case, and I couldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember who was in charge of logistics in Vlasenica for your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, it was Zoran Stupar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we call up in e-court now a part of the transcript from the Popovic case marked 65 ter 1D1090, page 14041, lines from 21 through line 6 on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At some point we'll have to move to the following page, but before we do that I would like to read certain passages. So, sir, in the Popovic case the Prosecution had called Dragan Todorovic as a witness, he was a member of your unit, and he was examined by my learned friend Mr. McCloskey. And his evidence ran as follows: The question by Mr. McCloskey was: "Among this group that you've named that left, do you know who was in charge of the group?" Todorovic answers: "Franc Kos, who was a 2nd lieutenant, signed for the equipment. If he was not around, Drazen Erdemovic had the rank of sergeant, and he would have to sign because privates could not sign. Their signature meant nothing. "Q. And you mentioned that Drazen Erdemovic joined this group a bit later. Can you tell us more about it? Do you know under what circumstances Erdemovic joined the group?" He answers, and we have to move to the following page: "Well, quite simply so that he wouldn't stay alone in the unit, because everybody would go to their homes if their homes were close. One part of the intervention group that was at the ready had already left. So as he was not going to Bijeljina, he joined the group that left the base." Does the evidence of this witness refresh your memory, first of all, in the sense that it says you were treated as a sergeant at the time, and perhaps you even signed the document on drawing supplies that were issued to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take it step-by-step what you put to the witness in detail, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So my first question: Does this passage, where the witness in the Popovic case says that it was either Franc Kos or you as 2nd lieutenant and sergeant respectively signed that list drawing supplies, weapons, ammunition, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you please read exactly the portions you would like to put to the witness. Let me start with the first: "France Kos, who was a 2nd lieutenant, signed for the equipment." That apparently is not a question but something put to the witness. "If hadn't be there," it does not say what or who had not been there, "it would have been Drazen Erdemovic who would have signed for a document like this." That is what the witness says and not as you phrased it. Does this -- did you ever sign a document like that in the absence of Mr. Kos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I had signed any document at all, I'm 100 per cent sure it would have been produced here and shown to me. I never signed anything that had anything to do with withdrawing weapons or being issued with weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you misrepresented the evidence of the witness, what you just read in your questions. Now, is there anything else you would like to put to the witness in order to see whether it refreshes his memory? If you do so, please do it literally and not in vague terms. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I know the practice is sometimes they get the audio of the Serbian, so that may be the explanation, because I know -- as you know, he's reading from the Serbian, so that may be what the glitch is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case, then it should be verified. Let me see. We have a -- one second, please. Yes. First of all, if there's any doubt as to what was -- what is written down in English deviates in any way from what is written down in B/C/S, then we would have to verify it. Mr. Stojanovic, I take it that within your team there's sufficient knowledge to make a first assessment of any discrepancies. Perhaps you could take the next break to look at that, the next break by the way is about to start anyhow. So please compare what is there in B/C/S and in English, see whether there's a -- any discrepancy. If so, we'd like to be informed about it. If not, please stick very much to what the witness really said, because that's not what you put to -- have put to this witness, at least on the basis of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One request, Your Honour, with your leave. Could you just tell me where is the misrepresentation of the witness's evidence in my question to this witness in order for me to address it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness talked about the potential situation, and you are putting it as if either of the two would sign it. That is -- and the witness was talking about such documents, not this document. A literal reading will make clear to you that it's not exactly the same. Not to say that you intentionally did so, Mr. Stojanovic, but read it carefully and you'll find out, or discuss it with your colleagues. If there is any doubt remains, then of course you are free to address the Chamber at any point in time. We -- in order to allow the witness to leave the courtroom, we will move into closed session and take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I take the opportunity to put on the record that as discussed in closed session the Defence will file its expedited response to a 92 ter motion in relation to Christopher Lawrence by the 10th of July. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: With your leave, Your Honour, in keeping with the instructions you gave us, we have tried to compare the English version of the transcript and the transcript which is the official transcript based on the audio recording of the evidence of this witness, and we have found significant discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Work should be done on that. It is not the official document. Still, the official document is the English version, and if there's any translation error, then of course it should be corrected, but the B/C/S transcription from the audio is not an official document of this Tribunal, although it may be very helpful, and we're all glad that these transcripts do exist. Then it should be -- it should be verified whether the B/C/S audio is translated accurately in English and whether the English transcript accurately reflects what is the accurate translation. That is the work that should be done. And we can't do it at this very moment. Again it seems to be not an issue which is central to the evidence of this witness, but if you have any questions or if it's clear to you how any confusion could be avoided or corrected, you please do so, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. When I tender this exhibit, I will also ask at the same time for this confusion to be addressed, because obviously you were not able to see in English what I was reading from the B/C/S. So the misunderstanding and the confusion are quite understandable, and I understand your objection. I will continue, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to add one thing, and I'm also addressing the Prosecution. The issue was raised not long ago, I think, and we asked for submissions by the Defence on the matter, if the witness attests to the accuracy of his testimony, then he does so on the basis of the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll discuss this matter later. The Chamber might want to discuss it among themselves as well. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Then we will tender this part of the transcript later when we have seen what the witness really said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience, Witness. Let me ask you this now: Do you remember that at any point you told anyone that you wanted to go on that mission of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: With your leave, I would call up again 65 ter 1D1091, which is again the testimony of Witness Dragan Todorovic, page 2402 -- 24204, excuse me, lines 1 through 23. Witness Todorovic in his evidence says, among other things: "Q. Thank you. And he addressed whom? "A. He addressed Obrenovic, and I later found out why --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you continue to read, it's for the Chamber important to know who "he" is, otherwise it's difficult to understand. Was Mr. Todorovic talking about Mr. Erdemovic at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He was talking about Pelemis, Your Honour, and the context is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know, and therefore what you usually would do is to also include the previous page. Now, you have uploaded only one page, so I can't look one page back, but apparently you say that the previous part of the transcript makes clear that Mr. Todorovic is testifying about Mr. Pelemis. That's -- then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I will begin here."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: "Q. And then he turned to Gojkovic and asked for a couple of soldiers because they were supposed to carry out a mission." And the witness answers: "Yes." "Q. France Kos, was he a lieutenant? Was he at the base at the time? "A. Yes. He took up that role on himself. "Q. Was Franc Kos a Slovene? "A. Yes." And now the crux of my question: "Q. Was Drazen Erdemovic there? "A. Erdemovic was with me in Trebinje but he volunteered. He was not forced to go. He was a sergeant. That was his rank." Now I ask you, Witness which if any part of this evidence by Todorovic is consistent with your memory; namely, did you really volunteer to go on that mission?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. It says here that I was with him in Trebinje and that I volunteered what, to go with him to Trebinje? What are you asking?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, there's talk about a mission. Now, you were kind enough to tell us that "he" is Mr. Pelemis, although that doesn't appear from the transcript itself. You left out a few lines. That seems to be no major problem either. It was about quarreling about something. And then he spoke to Gojkovic. It's not -- let's just assume that that is again Mr. Pelemis. And then later it is about a mission of which the transcript doesn't tell us what mission it is. The only thing it says, that Mr. Erdemovic was with the "he" in Trebinje and that he volunteered. But again, not volunteering to what. He was not forced to go -- forced to go where, to do what? It's totally unclear without further context. So therefore, I do understand that the witness is unable to answer this question which is so unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will -- I will try to deal with it with a different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Witness, that you at any point asked to go on that mission yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The one you got on the 16th. On the 16th of July, in the morning, you received a new assignment. We discussed this. The assignment was conveyed to you by Brano Gojkovic, and you concluded that it was from Pelemis. I'm asking you about that mission. Did you at any point express your readiness to go on that mission voluntarily?
